title: Predawn kernel checklist & quick triage
content:
Short context:
Predawn quick-scrub for the p99 KV-cache spike that cropped up yesterday evening. This is a lightweight personal checklist + hypotheses I want to test before standup. Not polished — just the steps I can run and hand off.

Observed symptoms (recap):
- p99 increased from ~95ms to ~420ms for short-seq requests (<= 64 tokens) between 21:40–22:05 UTC.
- CPU on host gpu-node-07 spiked, nvlink stable, GPU utilization steady (~68%).
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 92% -> 37% for the affected model bundle.
- Ticket INF-1427 created by SRE with initial trace links.

Immediate quick checklist (what I will run now):
1) Pull traces and sample requests:
   - grep for request ids in INF-1427 trace dump; sample 10 requests across the window.
   - command: curl -s "https://traces.internal/runs?ticket=INF-1427" | jq .entries[:10]
2) Check KV cache stats on the node:
   - ssh gpu-node-07; sudo journalctl -u redwood-kv-cache -n 200
   - run: /opt/redwood/bin/kv-stats --summarize --since 2026-03-11T20:00
3) Profile micro-batching behavior for the short-seq path:
   - enable verbose batching logs for model xg-13; tail /var/log/redwood/batching-xg-13.log
   - look for sudden batch size changes or long queue-wait durations.
4) Verify recent rollout/versions:
   - check model pinning: /api/internal/models/xg-13/releases -> last 24h.
   - PR to inspect: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/912 (last merged changes touched cache eviction heuristics)

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: recent eviction threshold change (PR 912) made cache too aggressive for short-context requests -> hit-rate collapse -> backend cold-starts and CPU pressure.
- H2: A burst of low-entropy requests caused batching to eager-merge sequences, increasing per-request CPU while lowering effective cache reuse.
- H3: Memory pressure on the node triggered out-of-band GC in the cache process; this caused lock contention and log stuttering.

Quick experiments to run (non-prod where possible):
- Experiment A (rollback heuristics): temporarily revert eviction policy on a canary pool and measure hit-rate (target 2h window). Owner: me (Devon).
- Experiment B (force larger batching cap): in staging, increase batch cap by +25% for xg-13 and replay sampled requests; compare latency distributions. Owner: Marcus.
- Experiment C (throttle background compaction): set compaction backoff to 30s and observe if CPU tail reduces. Owner: Lina.

Short commands / sanity checks I keep handy:
- kv-stats quick: /opt/redwood/bin/kv-stats --node gpu-node-07 --last 2h | grep -E "hit_rate|evictions|mem_used"
- live tail: ssh gpu-node-07 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-kv-cache -f --since "10 minutes ago"'
- batch log query: rg "queue_wait_ms|batch_size" /var/log/redwood/batching-xg-13.log | tail -n 200

Notes to self / red flags to call out in standup:
- If hit-rate recovers after reverting PR 912, call for urgent rollback and postmortem (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- If CPU tail persists despite hit-rate normalization, escalate to SRE for node-level investigation (thermal throttling / driver bug).
- Document any sampling instructions so CS can reproduce for customer cases.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Did any jobs (backups, compactions) overlap the 21:30–22:10 window on gpu-node-07? Check cron and k8s jobs.
- Are there per-tenant cache size anomalies? The tenant heatmap showed one tenant with a large growth spike at 21:38. Who owns that tenant? Add to linked_artifacts if found.
- Is there an observable correlation between request size and eviction rate in the period? Need a small script to join request size and cache eviction events.

Next steps (today):
- Run Experiment A in canary; log results to INF-1427. (Devon, today by 11:00 PT)
- Ask Lina to run compaction backoff test in staging and report CPU delta. (Lina, today)
- Marcus to run replay with increased batch cap and post latency histograms. (Marcus, today/tonight)

If I get a clean short fix (rollback heuristic) I'll open an incident note and propose patch + gradual rollout. If not, schedule a follow-up deep-dive with kernel + SRE.

Scratchpad: quick todo bullets (personal)
- [ ] Run kv-stats on gpu-node-07 (done? no)
- [ ] Push canary rollback branch (branch: devon/evict-roll-back)
- [ ] Create short repro script to join traces + cache events (filename: devon/repro/join-traces-evict.sh)
- [ ] Add experimental flags to runtime to toggle eviction_threshold at runtime (feature flag path: /flags/evict-threshold)

Raw log snippets I might paste in ticket (save these):
- "2026-03-12T21:42:05Z cache_evict: tenant=acme size=42 evicted=120 total_mem=3.2GB"
- "2026-03-12T21:43:18Z batch_queue wait_ms=76 batch_size=1"

End of quick notes. Will tidy up after experiments and attach links to INF-1427.

-- Devon B.
